comparisons.peer_topic: Shareholder Returns and Stock Repurchase Program
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD returned $862 million to shareholders in 2024 through stock repurchases, with $4.7 billion remaining available under a program that has no termination date and may be suspended or discontinued at any time.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD disclose their 2024 share repurchase activities, including the amount spent, shares repurchased, and remaining authorization. However, the scale and structure differ significantly. AMD repurchased 5.9 million shares for $862 million, leaving $4.7 billion available. In contrast, NVDA repurchased 21 million shares for $9.7 billion, leaving $22.5 billion available. Additionally, NVDA explicitly stated the program aims to offset dilution, while AMD noted its program has no termination date and may be suspended. AMD did not mention post-year-end repurchases in this specific disclosure summary, whereas NVDA detailed repurchases of 2.8 million shares for $1.9 billion in early 2024 under a 10b5-1 plan.

sentences.text: During fiscal year 2024, we repurchased 21 million shares of our common stock for $9.7 billion.
From January 29, 2024 through February 16, 2024, we repurchased 2.8 million shares for $1.9 billion pursuant to a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan.
Our share repurchase program aims to offset dilution from shares issued to employees.
During the twelve months ended December 28, 2024, we returned a total of $862 million to shareholders through the repurchase of 5.9 million shares of common stock under our stock repurchase program.
As of December 28, 2024, $4.7 billion remained available for future stock repurchases under this program.
The stock repurchase program does not obligate us to acquire any common stock, has no termination date and may be suspended or discontinued at any time.
